fields.features_heading: What a Blank Request Form Leaves Undecided
fields.features_subheading: A PDF collects the idea. Who reviews it, which budget pays for it, and when the work could start are still settled in someone's inbox.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that fit the request type

Show each request type its own fields. An IT request asks which systems the project touches, while a facilities request asks for the building and for photos of the leak or damage.
fields.feature_2:
Sign-off before the intake meeting

Send a request to its sponsor or data owner before it reaches the intake meeting. The sign-off is recorded with a name and a time, and the request then moves on to the next step.
fields.feature_3:
Routing by estimated cost

Route each request by its estimate. Work under your line becomes a work order, larger jobs go to the budget committee, and the requester can see which path the request has taken.
fields.feature_4:
Rush flags on short deadlines

Compare the requested due date with the lead time the work needs. A deadline that is too short is marked rush and waits for a manager to approve it, instead of jumping the queue.
fields.feature_5:
Ranking against team hours

Score each request on the criteria your board picked, then rank it against this quarter's team hours. The board sees which requests fit now and which ones wait for the next round.
fields.feature_6:
Your intake app, in your repo

Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. The routing rules and every past request then live in a codebase you control, ready to extend or host elsewhere.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Intake Desks and the Rules They Run
fields.tab_content_1:
Registrar sign-off comes before IT sees the request

Westbrook College's IT office runs every new project through one form. Admissions wants campus tour sign-ups to create applicant records. The form asks which systems the work touches, and the answer includes the student records system. Registrar Dana Ortiz signs off first, before IT's Thursday intake meeting.
fields.tab_content_2:
Capital planning gets any estimate over $50,000

Lakeview County's parks department needs a new roof on the Elm Street community center. The request carries photos of the leak and an $84,000 contractor estimate. Facilities turns anything under $50,000 into a work order. This one is over the line and goes to the capital planning committee.
fields.tab_content_3:
Rush review for signage due in 9 business days

Harlow Outfitters' brand studio needs 15 business days to produce in-store signage. The retail team asks for window posters for a weekend sale that opens in 9 business days. The form counts the days as the date is picked and marks the request rush. Creative director Marcus Bell approves it or offers a later date.
fields.tab_content_4:
The quarter's 1,200 hours go to the top four requests

Maple Ridge Health's project office scores every request out of 25 for value, urgency, and effort. Requests are funded in score order until the quarter's 1,200 team hours run out. Four requests fit in 1,150 hours. The patient portal redesign scored 17 of 25 and needs 300 hours. It waits for next quarter.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Project Request Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to make a project request form that puts every request before the person who approves it and ranks the rest by score.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Name the person who says yes
fields.howto_step_1_des: Gather the last 20 requests that came in, wherever they arrived, by email or in a hallway conversation. Note what you had to ask each requester afterward. Those follow-up questions are the fields your current form is missing.
fields.howto_step_2_des: For each kind of request, write down who approves it, such as a data owner or a budget holder. When a request needs two approvals, put them in order, and let the second approver read the first one's note before deciding.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Turn habits into thresholds the form can apply. Estimates over $50,000 go to capital planning, and deadlines under 15 business days are rush. Words like large or urgent get argued over in every meeting, while a number settles it.
fields.howto_step_4_des: If more requests arrive than the people doing the work can take on, agree on a score before the form goes live. Weigh the value of each request against the effort it needs, and the review board gets a ranked list it can defend.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your fields and rules into one prompt. Emergent builds the request form, with a database that holds every request and the routing between approvers. When a rule changes later, describe the new rule in a sentence.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Give each requester a status page, plus an email whenever the request changes step or someone leaves a note. Requesters who can check the status for themselves stop writing to the intake inbox to ask where things stand.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Send a few old requests through it
fields.howto_step_7_des: Re-enter five of the requests from step 1 and check where each one lands. Every request should reach the approver you would have picked by hand. Fix any rule that sends one elsewhere before you share the form.

faq_plan.q: What is a project request form?
faq_plan.a: A project request form is how someone in an organization proposes new work before anyone agrees to take it on. It records what is needed and why, the target date, and the sponsor backing it. The office that receives it uses those answers to decide whether the project goes ahead, and when.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a project request form?
faq_plan.a: Start from the decisions made about every request: who approves it, which budget pays, and how many hours the work needs. Ask only for the facts those decisions use. Then describe the fields and the rules to Emergent's AI form builder, which builds the form and the database that holds each request.

faq_plan.q: Is a project intake form the same as a project request form?
faq_plan.a: They can be one form under two names. Where they differ, the requester fills in the request, and intake covers the screening and scheduling that follow. A project intake form then adds fields only the reviewing office completes, such as the hours estimate and the score.

faq_plan.q: What should I change in a project intake form template before using it?
faq_plan.a: Change the routing first. A project intake form template gives you the layout, but it cannot know who approves what where you work, or above which budget. Write those rules down, then cut any field no decision uses. Intake in other fields follows the same test: a life coaching intake form asks only what the first session needs.

faq_plan.q: What does a sample project intake form ask?
faq_plan.a: A sample project intake form asks who is requesting, what problem the project solves, the target date, and a rough budget. Add a question on which systems or sites the work touches, because that answer decides who signs off. Make the sponsor field required. Every request should name someone who will back it.

faq_plan.q: What happens after a project request form is approved?
faq_plan.a: It becomes a scheduled project with an owner, a start date, and its hours set aside. For a larger project, write a charter next. In the California Department of Technology's project guidance, the drafted charter goes to the executive sponsor for approval. Keep the original request linked to the project as the record of why it was approved.

faq_plan.q: How should a project request form score requests?
faq_plan.a: Pick a few criteria the review board agrees on, such as value and effort, and give each a fixed weight before requests start arriving. Ask for an hours estimate too. The ranked list can then be cut where the available hours run out. A fitness assessment form works on the same idea: a few measured items add up to one number someone can act on.

faq_plan.q: Who should approve requests from a project request form?
faq_plan.a: Route each request to the person who owns what it changes: the data owner for a system, or the budget holder for spending above a set line. Name one approver per request type, and put two in order when both are needed. In an app built with Emergent, each sign-off can send a Slack or email alert to the next approver.

faq_plan.q: How should a project request form handle rush deadlines?
faq_plan.a: Publish the lead time next to the date field. Requesters then see that signage takes 15 business days before they pick a date. Count business days and leave holidays out. A date shorter than the lead time still goes through, marked rush, for a manager to accept or move.

faq_plan.q: Should one project request form cover every kind of request?
faq_plan.a: One form works well as long as it branches by request type. An IT project and a renovation need different questions, and each type should see only its own fields. An app built with Emergent keeps every request, whatever its type, in a database you own. Some requests belong elsewhere: a company offsite fits an event planning form better than project review.
